Outered to the transient package, as UMG does: an operation outlives the widget that made it, and a recycled list row mid-drag is the ordinary case.
Addressed by DreamGUI user index rather than by a raw controller, so split screen does not have to rediscover which player a menu belongs to.
A Slate focus change, not a DreamGUI one. UDreamWidget::ClearKeyboardFocus is the framework-level counterpart and the two are usually wanted together.

UMG's Draw* family writes into an FPaintContext handed to a Blueprint OnPaint override. There is no immediate-mode paint pass here: a DreamGUI widget draws by owning a mesh, so anything drawn is a widget with a visual on it rather than a call inside a paint.
See DrawBox.

FEventReply is Slate's reply object, built by a handler and returned to Slate. A DreamGUI handler answers a bool meaning 'let this keep bubbling' (the IDreamPointer* interfaces), so there is no reply object to construct.
See Handled.
There is no capture to take: a pressed pointer's PressWidget already receives every drag and the release wherever the pointer travels. UDreamWidget::HasMouseCapture reports that state.
See CaptureMouse.
Separate from the input mode on purpose there: re-setting the whole input mode to change only the lock is how a project takes focus away from its own menu.
EMouseLockMode::DoNotLock.
A verb on the widget rather than a reply built inside a handler.

A verb rather than UMG's FEventReply builder. Viewport pixels, the same space GetMousePositionOnViewport reports and a geometry's absolute coordinates are in, so 'warp the cursor onto this widget' is one conversion and not two.

UMG makes a handler arm drag detection for a key. Here the pointer pipeline detects drags itself against a distance and hold threshold (UDreamEventSystem's drag settings), so there is nothing for a handler to arm -- what a source supplies is the drag's MEANING, which is CreateDragDropOperation plus BeginDragWithOperation.
See DetectDrag.
The pipeline ends a drag when the pointer is released; a handler has no reply to end it through. CancelDragDrop is the verb for ending one early.
Per pointer, because several fingers can drag at once on a touch screen; pointer 0 is the mouse.
Takes any resource the brush can draw, which here includes sprites and atlases as well as textures and materials.
Zero width or height keeps the brush's own size rather than collapsing it.

Same verb on this framework's brush: a FDreamUIImageBrush holding a material is rewritten to hold a dynamic instance of it, which is returned; one already holding an instance returns it; a texture or sprite brush returns null. The brush is a value, so the caller hands it back to the image (UDreamImage::SetBrush). Not the same as a rect block's material, which belongs to the draw call and is deliberately not handed out (see Border.json).

Walks the world's menu anchors and closes the open ones, skipping class defaults and archetypes. Walks rather than keeping a registry of open anchors: an anchor closed by any other route would have to remember to leave such a registry, and the one that forgot would leak a phantom. Returns how many it closed, so a caller can tell 'nothing was open' from 'did nothing'.

Reads UDreamUIManagerWorldSubsystem's registered-widget array, which is the only honest source: widgets are UObjects outered to a widget tree, so an actor iterator cannot see them and an object iterator would also sweep up archetypes, designer previews and other worlds.
Widget classes only; a behaviour implementing the interface is found through the widget's GetComponentByInterface.

FKeyEvent and friends are Slate's input structs, delivered to SWidget handlers. Input arrives here as a UDreamPointerEventData or UDreamKeyEventData from the event system, so there is no Slate event to unwrap.
See GetInputEventFromKeyEvent.

Returns false when Slate is not running, so 'no inset needed' and 'could not ask' are not both a zero. UMG's SpillOverPadding is not returned: nothing here draws outside the viewport rect to spill over it.

An engine-wide renderer simulation switch that happens to sit in UMG's library. It is not a widget-framework concern and the engine already exposes it; DreamGUI wrapping it would be a second door onto the same global.
Registers a cursor SHAPE with the platform. DreamGUI's Cursor property picks among the shapes a project has registered and does not own the registry.
The game window's title bar is a Slate window concern. DreamGUI draws inside the viewport and has no window chrome of its own.
